- Use Read, Edit, Write, Glob, Grep. Bash only for `./scripts/run-test.sh ...`, read-only `git status|diff|log`, `ls`, `mkdir`. cd to the repository root in each Bash command.
- Write only `tests/cost_effects.gd` (and its log via the wrapper). Never edit effects/, entities/, game/, previews/, shaders/, scripts/, or existing tests. Do not commit. If a command fails or is refused, say so; never print expected output instead of a real run.

Read the README's account of the recorded mistake (the cost script reported the same ms for every case, an empty scene included: it measured itself). Make sure your instrument can tell cases apart: e.g. check `OS.low_processor_usage_mode` / its sleep, compare wall-clock frame time with `Performance.get_monitor(Performance.TIME_PROCESS)` / `TIME_PHYSICS_PROCESS`, and keep an empty-scene control. Explain which number you report and why.
- Cases (CHANGE-BRIEF.md "Price predictions and budget"): (1) empty scene (a bare Node); (2) the game scene (`res://game/main.tscn` or a `GameManager` like the existing tests, on a real floor — use `fixed_map_seed` and `game.seed_rng(seed)`; 萨米 `snow` has fire pits) with both effects off: no HitSpark alive and every FirePit unlit (burn_left 0); (3) Effect A at the brief's peak, 8 `HitSpark` instances alive at once under the GameManager (instancing `res://effects/hit_spark.tscn` directly is fine for the price — it is a measurement fixture, not the gameplay event; note they free themselves after 0.55 s, so re-instance to keep 8 alive through the timed window and say how); (4) Effect B heaviest: the brief prices one pit at ratio 1.0 and four pits — fuel the floor's pits to ≥ 120 s through `feed()` in the fixture (measurement setup, not a state test) and report both one-pit and all-pits if the floor has fewer than four, say how many. Report mean and spread (e.g. stdev or min–max over repeats) per case, the frame count, and warm-up. If cases that should differ read the same, say so.
- Run exactly `./scripts/run-test.sh cost_effects.gd 60 300` and show the real output. Then state, against CHANGE-BRIEF.md's predictions (A +0.02 ms, B +0.005/+0.02 ms headless over control; GPU budgets 0.25/0.15 ms are compared on GPU time, not this), what the numbers say and do not say, and why a GPU effect's headless price is near zero.

Read CLAUDE.md first. Adapt the chapter's cost script from Example 09
into tests/cost_effects.gd for the effects in CHANGE-BRIEF.md.

scene with both effects off; Effect A at the most bursts the brief says
can be alive at once; and Effect B in its heaviest state. Report each
case's mean and spread. If two cases that should differ report the
same value, say so: the script may be measuring itself. Do not change
any effect or gameplay file. Run it with
./scripts/run-test.sh cost_effects.gd 60 300 and show the real output.
Do not commit.

input.message:
I wrote `tests/cost_effects.gd` and ran `./scripts/run-test.sh cost_effects.gd 60 300` for real. It exits 0. The script tells the empty scene and the game scene apart easily: 0.0032 ms against 7.68 ms, about 2,400 times apart, so it is not measuring itself. But none of the three effect cases can be told apart from the game with both effects off. A three-pit fire and a no-fire control land on effectively the same number, inside the control's noise.

It is the only file I wrote; the wrapper also wrote its log to `logs/cost_effects_60fps.log`. No effect, gameplay, shader or script file was touched, and nothing was committed (the folder is not a git repository). The first run failed with two GDScript type-inference parse errors; I fixed them and reran. After that full run I changed only the instrument checks and report format, then ran it once more. The numbers below are from that final run.

**What happened in the chapter example, and how this script avoids it.** Without `--fixed-fps`, headless Godot pauses about 6.9 ms every frame (`low_processor_usage_mode_sleep_usec` = 6900), so the example timed that pause for every case. Here:
- **Pause check:** the script prints the pause settings (low-processor mode false, pause 6900 µs, `max_fps` 0, window cannot draw). It warns if the empty scene's frame comes anywhere near 6.9 ms. It came out at 0.0032 ms, so no pause is in the timing.
- **Command line:** `OS.get_cmdline_args()` printed only `--script ...`, because Godot does not list engine options such as `--fixed-fps`. So the pause is ruled out from the timing above, not from the command line.
- **Frame count:** each 300-sample window advanced exactly 300 engine frames (299 physics ticks, an off-by-one in where the tick counter is read).
- **Rejected cross-check:** I tried `Performance.TIME_PROCESS` + `TIME_PHYSICS_PROCESS`, and they are not per-frame values here. Their sum (about 13.8 ms) was larger than the 7.7 ms frame. Physics also read a frozen 3.591 ms (6.373 ms in the first run) throughout the empty scene. They are printed for reference only.

**Which number I report.** Wall-clock time between consecutive frames: one full frame of CPU work (physics, process, and the stand-in renderer's sync). Each case gets 60 warm-up frames, then 300 timed frames, repeated 5 times. The four game cases are interleaved and their order rotated each round, because the live floor (89 enemies, threat build-up) drifts over time. Each effect is also compared with the no-effects control from the same round ("paired" below).

**Cases.**
- **Empty:** a bare Node.
- **Game, effects off:** `game/main.tscn` with `fixed_map_seed` and `seed_rng(2026)`, on a 萨米 floor 1 with 3 fire pits and 89 enemies. No HitSpark alive and all pits out (`burn_left` 0). The player's health is reset every frame so she survives.
- **A, 8 sparks:** 8 HitSpark instances under the GameManager. Each frees itself after 0.55 s (33 frames), so the script adds a new one on the frame after one is freed. They are staggered one every 4 frames during warm-up. At most points 7–8 were alive, 73 were added per window (about 0.24 a frame), and that adding is included in the price.
- **B, one pit:** one pit fuelled with `feed(300)`; it was still at `burn_left` 294 at the end.
- **B, all pits:** the floor has 3 pits, not the 4 the brief prices for. All three were fuelled the same way and ended at 294.

**Real output (summary part):**
```
case        mean      sd_rep   min-max(rep)         frame_sd   nodes   vs game_off
empty        0.0032   0.0001    0.0031-0.0033      0.0006       2    -7.6728
game_off     7.6759   0.0498    7.6219-7.7395      0.7014    4631    +0.0000
A_8          7.7008   0.0606    7.6214-7.7897      0.7003    4667    +0.0248
B_1          7.6627   0.0446    7.6019-7.7259      0.6695    4636    -0.0132
B_all(3)     7.7380   0.1336    7.5868-7.9421      0.7726    4634    +0.0621
PAIRED (case minus game_off in the same round; mean, sd, min-max over 5 rounds)
  A_8     +0.0248 ms  sd 0.0287  min-max -0.0052..+0.0581  -> within 2 standard errors of zero: not distinguishable from game_off
  B_1     -0.0132 ms  sd 0.0777  min-max -0.1376..+0.0535  -> within 2 standard errors of zero: not distinguishable from game_off
  B_all   +0.0621 ms  sd 0.1138  min-max -0.0418..+0.2464  -> within 2 standard errors of zero: not distinguishable from game_off
CHECK empty (0.0032 ms) and game_off (7.6759 ms) differ by 2426x: the instrument sees the scene
CHECK empty frame 0.0032 ms << 6.900 ms sleep: no frame sleep in the timing
COST_EFFECTS DONE
```
The full per-round output is in `logs/cost_effects_60fps.log`.

**Cases that read the same.** Empty and game clearly differ. The effect cases do not differ from the control, but the setup did change: node counts went up by about 36 with 8 sparks, the pits were really lit, and the sparks were really alive. So "the same" here means the effect's CPU price is below this game's frame-to-frame noise (about 0.7 ms per frame, 0.05–0.13 ms between rounds). It does not mean the timer is broken. The one-pit case even came out below the control (−0.013 ms), which is noise.
